headline: High-risk data and instruction flow: Copilot can write repo context while MemMachine exposes MCP/API surfaces, creating default-path leakage and cascading-error risk.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Copilot reads repo context and open editor buffers and can write filesystem edits; MemMachine exposes an MCP server and conversational context. That creates a plausible bridge where attacker-controlled content from one side can be treated as instructions by the other, even though no direct shared channel is documented. Uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF MemMachine content is copied into repo files or editor buffers that Copilot reads
IF an MCP-connected workflow forwards Copilot-generated text into MemMachine prompts without provenance checks
mitigations: Disable automatic ingestion of untrusted text into either agent's prompt context
Require explicit human review before copying outputs between agents
Tag all cross-agent content with provenance labels
Restrict MemMachine MCP tools to read-only during evaluation
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and instruction-stripping at the bridge

B_data_leakage.rationale: Copilot touches source code and open editor buffers and sends requests to api.githubcopilot.com; MemMachine handles long-term user facts and conversational context via REST/Python/MCP. If the same workspace or prompt bridge carries sensitive code or personal facts, both agents can leak data across their respective backends. The shared workspace is not documented, so uncertainty remains but the pathway is plausible.
conditions: IF the same files or prompts contain secrets, credentials, or personal facts
IF outputs from one agent are forwarded into the other's API or MCP context
mitigations: Keep sensitive files out of shared editor buffers
Use separate workspaces for code and personal-memory tasks
Block secrets from being pasted into either agent
Review outbound traffic destinations for both agents
requires-engineering: enforce redaction before cross-agent forwarding

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Copilot can write the filesystem and modify git state, while MemMachine exposes API/MCP access but no filesystem write is documented. A direct write-write conflict is not evidenced; the main overlap is indirect coordination through shared content, so the blast radius is limited and the safer severity is low.
conditions: IF MemMachine is configured to mutate shared files through an external bridge
IF Copilot Workspace applies edits to the same git branch while MemMachine also writes via an MCP-connected tool
mitigations: Assign separate branches or directories per agent
Pause one agent before the other writes shared artifacts
Use human merge review for all git changes
Limit MemMachine to read-only retrieval during coding sessions

D_cascading_error.rationale: Copilot can propose edits in Workspace, and MemMachine can consume conversational context through API/MCP. If MemMachine treats Copilot output as authoritative, an error or hallucination can cascade into downstream planning or actions. No verification layer is documented in the pair, so the interaction is plausible in default use but not proven dangerous enough for high.
conditions: IF Copilot-generated text is forwarded into MemMachine without independent verification
IF MemMachine uses that text as a source of truth for subsequent recommendations or actions
mitigations: Require a verification step before MemMachine consumes Copilot output
Mark Copilot output as untrusted draft text
Compare critical facts against primary sources
Keep action-taking disabled until human approval
requires-engineering: add provenance-aware confidence scoring

E_compliance.rationale: Copilot is a closed-source GitHub service handling source code and repo context, while MemMachine is an open-source agent handling long-term user facts and conversational context. The profiles do not show a direct residency or certification mismatch, but mixed retention and logging policies are plausible and should be checked before sharing regulated data. The other agent is cited because the risk is pairwise data flow.
conditions: IF regulated personal data or customer data is placed into both agents
IF their retention or logging settings differ for the same data class
mitigations: Avoid placing regulated data in shared prompts
Review each vendor's retention settings
Document which data classes each agent may process
Separate compliance-sensitive workflows from coding workflows
